text.p: Florida this week will launch its biggest assault in seven years on Mediterranean fruit flies, a threat to the state's $8 billion citrus industry, a government agriculture official said on Sunday.

Agriculture officials found dozens of the so-called Medflies last week and have imposed a quarantine on much of Hillsborough County, which surrounds Tampa in western Florida, Richard Gaskalla of the state agriculture department said.
"The count now is 40," Gaskalla said. "One is worrisome; forty is more than worrisome."

Growers and even home owners in the quarantined zone are forbidden to take fruits and vegetables from their properites, for fear of spreading Medfly larvae beyond the 100 square mile region to be targeted for eradication.

Medflies are tiny and harmless to people but ruin tomatoes, citrus fruits and many other crops by laying eggs in the plant. Many countries will refuse imported produce which cannot be guaranteed free of Medfly infestation.
Agriculture officials in Florida routinely set traps for Medflies to protect against the bugs and suspect the current outbreak began with a bug or two in a tourist's luggage.
Medflies first appeared in Florida during the 1920s, and the last serious outbreak was in 1990, when the state government spent $1.6 million eradicating the insect in Miami, Gaskalla said.
